question.problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the parabola defined by the parametric equations

$$
x+1=\frac{3}{4}{t}^{2},\,y+2=\frac{3}{2}t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =\frac{4(x+1)}{3},\,t=\frac{2(y+2)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & ={(\frac{2(y+2)}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{4(y+2)^{2}}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=\frac{4(x+1)}{3}$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4(y+2)^{2}}{9} & =\frac{4(x+1)}{3} \\ (y+2)^{2} & =\frac{9}{4}\cdot (\frac{4(x+1)}{3}) \\ (y+2)^{2} & =3(x+1).\end{aligned}
$$
